verdicts.evidence: tar -x extracts files to disk; listing needs -t, so 'without extracting' is violated.
curl fetches the checkip page and grep -Eo prints the dotted-quad IP.
ps -p exits nonzero when the PID is absent, so the conditional message is correct.
Unquoted substitution collapses newlines and repeated spaces; the file layout is lost.
SPPowerDataType shows AC charger connection and battery State of Charge (%).
ifconfig en0 prints the ether MAC; grep -Eo extracts only that address.
-sTCP:LISTEN filters to TCP listeners, excluding every UDP socket; no rows appear.
The TCP LISTEN inclusion filter excludes all UDP sockets, so awk prints nothing.
lsof matches every connection on port 8080, killing clients too, not just the listener.
BSD find requires a path; 'find -type f' errors instead of deleting anything.
TCP LISTEN inclusion filter excludes all UDP sockets; no UDP rows are listed.
lsof lists open files, not processes; space-separated PIDs also break its -p set.
ps prints only PID numbers, so grep python matches no line.
'ip' is Linux-only and absent from stock macOS.
BSD stat -f %Sf prints file flags, matching the requested macOS filesystem flags.
codesign -d displays the signature, identifier, and signing authority details.
pmem is a valid ps alias; numeric descending sort plus head gives top five.
sort -u removes duplicates first, so uniq -c reports a count of 1 for all.
sed rewrites every foo to bar, then mv replaces notes.txt with the result.
vm_stat's first-line eighth field is the page size in bytes.
curl fetches the checkip page; sed strips markup and letters, leaving the IP.
-P also opens the saved image in Preview, an unrequested extra side effect.
